case_title: RAMESH KUMAR SONI v. STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH
trial_court_outcome: Case was exclusively triable by the Court of Session
offence_finally_established: Offences punishable under Sections 408, 420, 467, 468 and 471 of the IPC
neutral_facts: The accused was charged with offences punishable under Sections 408, 420, 467, 468 and 471 of the IPC. A case was registered against the accused on 18th May, 2007. The offences in question were initially triable by a Magistrate of First Class. However, an amendment to the Code of Criminal Procedure in 2007 shifted the trial of these offences to the Court of Sessions. The accused filed an application seeking remission of the case for trial by a Judicial Magistrate, arguing that the amendment should not apply to cases pending before the amendment. The trial court held that since no charge-sheet had been filed before the Magistrate as on the date the amendment came into force, the case was exclusively triable by the Court of Session. The High Court affirmed this view, and the Supreme Court upheld the trial court's decision, stating that the amendment applied to cases instituted after the amendment came into force.
